plan.summary: This 1-4 block is a simple off-camp boxing S&C build with one 60-minute session each week. Week 1 establishes a baseline on a primary lower-body strength movement, then Weeks 2-3 build basic power, strength, trunk work, and conditioning with beginner-friendly bodyweight drills. Week 4 is a deload to reduce fatigue while keeping movement quality high. After this block, Weeks 5-8 will progress intensity carefully, and Weeks 9-12 will shift toward sharper speed and power expression without forcing a fight-camp peak.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic strength, power, trunk control, and conditioning with simple bodyweight work that supports boxing without excess soreness.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the same patterns with slightly harder variations and tighter density while keeping recovery manageable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and express it with faster, sharper, more reactive bodyweight power work.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a quiet landing. Reset between reps and stop if height drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler takeoff with less timing.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable box and step down each rep.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with easier split-squat sets, then work up to one hard clean set per side. Use this session to establish your current baseline for future progress. Keep your front foot flat and control the bottom.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your hardest clean set of 5-8 reps per side. Log the reps and difficulty so the app can track your baseline for later blocks.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set per side and note whether balance or leg strength was the limit.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the rear-foot-elevated version feels too unstable.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lower if you need more challenge without equipment.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 1-2 reps in reserve on each set. Keep the body straight and lower under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench or box if full push-ups are not clean yet.

substitutionOptions.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are too easy and shoulders feel good.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Pull the chest to the bar or edge, pause briefly, and keep the body rigid. Stop before form breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a sturdy table if no fixed bar is available.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Against Door
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if the setup is fully secure and controlled.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, squeeze glutes, and keep ribs down. End the set before your low back sags.

substitutionOptions.name: Body Saw Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if a standard plank is too easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Hardstyle Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use shorter harder holds if you prefer more tension.

exercises.name: Shadowboxing Conditioning Intervals
exercises.notes: Stay sharp and relaxed. Keep the feet active and the hands snapping back to guard.

endurancePrescription.progression: Focus on steady output in Week 1. Keep every round technically clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Split Squat

substitutionOptions.name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
